newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 23.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
INVESTIGATORS SEEK PERMISSION TO ARREST LALOO PRASAD YADAV

Officials of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) have sought permission from their headquarters to arrest Bihar Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav and two of his cabinet ministers in the fodder scam case. The team headed by a joint director of the CBI has informed the CBI chief that the custodial interrogation of Laloo Yadav and other politicians was necessary in the case.
The Economic Times
PLANS TO BOOST INFRASTRUCTURE SECTOR ANNOUNCED

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral announced a series of incentives to boost infrastructure development. A policy on corporatisation of major ports, making funds available for power projects, allowing state-owned power companies to expand equity base and setting up a monitoring cell to expedite the progress of power projects were among the plans disclosed. The government will clear 30 port projects soon. The Petroleum Ministry will work out a policy to help private parties to import liquid fuels. Documents on build-operate-transfer road projects will be made bankable.
GOVERNMENT TO GIVE UP CONTROL OVER BROADCAST MEDIA

The government has decided to give up its control over the national television network (Doordarshan) and the All India Radio (AIR) from September 15. These two media networks will thereafter be run by a corporation named Prasar Bharati. In effect this will give autonomy to the Doordarshan and the AIR. The government will also pass on all the assets and properties of the two networks to Prasar Bharati. Though the proposed corporation will be free from government control it will receive yearly grants from the government as equity, grant-in-aid or as loans.
Financial Express
NEW RESERVE BANK PLAN TO CHECK RUPEE APPRECIATION

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has devised a way to prevent the rupee from appreciating against the dollar without direct market intervention. It is entering into direct off-market deals with corporates. The RBI has already entered into a number of deals with a few banks. These banks sold dollars on behalf of their corporate clients. According to an estimate, the Reserve Bank on Tuesday struck off-market deals worth $25 million to $30 million. In the recent past the Reserve Bank has been regularly buying in the foreign exchange markets to stop the rupee from gaining strength against the greenback.
14-YEAR TAX EXEMPTION FOR FIAT'S AUTO PROJECT

The auto project of Italian auto giant Fiat to make Palio cars will get tax exemption for 14 years from the Maharashtra state government. The government will be giving up four billion rupees every year this way. The 20 billion rupee project will be set up at Ranjangaon in Pune district. The project is being promoted jointly by Italy's Fiat SpA and India's Vinod Doshi family. The state government has also agreed to allot 85 hectares of land for the Palio project at a concessional rate of 250 rupees per hectare.
Business Standard
BOURSE REGULATOR MAY REVIEW NATIONAL BOURSE STATUS

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) may soon induct brokers on the board of the National Stock Exchange (NSE). The SEBI has received representations from various associations of the NSE members in Bombay and Calcutta about the problems at the exchange and has decided to review them. The Delhi-based NSE Association recently wrote to the Finance Ministry asking for permission to elect half of the NSE board members and to nominate the remaining half.
GOVERNMENT OFFERS ENOUGH FUNDS FOR NEW POWER PROJECTS

The Finance Minister gave an open-ended offer that funds would not be a constraint for new power projects in the central (government) sector. The only limit will be the absorption capacity of the sector, he said. Power projects for which memoranda of understanding were signed will be closely monitored by the Power Ministry. All the necessary central clearances will be given before this December. The minister's offer followed a high profile meeting on the development of the infrastructure sector. Prime Minister Gujral listed power, surface transport, ports and petroleum sectors as the priority areas for his government.
The Observer
PANEL SUGGESTS MODIFICATIONS IN BOURSE DEALS

A committee in its report to the bourse regulator SEBI has recommended the abolition of the twin-track system segregating carry forward trades and delivery trades in equities. The report will be discussed by the SEBI board soon and its approval is expected by the second week of August. In the note he said it was a world-wide system of segregating transactions for futures from that of delivery. The committee has sought to do away with a few of the main features of the present revised carry forward system which is unpopular with the brokers.
CORE GROUP FORMED TO TACKLE ECONOMIC CRIMES

A core group was set up within the reconstituted economic Intelligence Council (EIC) to monitor the fast-changing trends in economic crimes. A meeting of the EIC reviewed the trends in economic crimes with special emphasis on areas and regions in the country where economic crimes are increasing. It also focussed on the sources and uses of black money.
